title: Annotatio IV §.X: Foecundus Hermianensis — improper speech; spiritual presence; mystery contains
pass_a_gloss: To Gelasius there votes the Bishop of Hermiane of the same Age, FOECUNDUS, flourishing in the time of the Emperor Justinian (see Petavius’s Rationarium of times, part 1, Book 7, ch. 7 and 8). He in the ninth Book of his Work signifies by these things the impropriety of Christ’s words equally and His Spiritual presence in the Sacred Eucharist: The SACRAMENT, he says, of the body and blood of Christ, which is in the consecrated bread and cup, we call His body and blood: Not that the bread is PROPERLY His body, and the cup blood, but that they contain in themselves the MYSTERY of body and blood — following namely the Doctrine, concerning the natural and local absence of Christ’s body on earth, of VIGILIUS Bishop of Trent, older than him by nearly thirty years,
pass_b_english: Foecundus of Hermiane (same age; Justinian’s time) seconds Gelasius: Christ’s words are improper speech; presence in the Eucharist is spiritual.

We call the sacrament in consecrated bread and cup His body and blood — not that bread is PROPERLY body or cup blood, but that they contain the MYSTERY — following Vigilius of Trent on the body’s natural local absence on earth.
source_text: Gelasio suffragatur ejusdem Seculi Episcopus Hermianensis FOECUNDUS, Justiniani Imperatoris tempore florens, (Vid. Petavii Rationarium tempor. part. 1. Lib. 7. cap. 7. & 8.) Hic Librô nonô Operis sui, improprietatem verborum Christi æquè ac Spiritualem ejus in S. Eucharistia præsentiam, hisce significatum it: SACRAMENTUM inquit, corporis & sanguinis Christi, quod est in pane & poculo consecrato, corpus ejus & sanguinem dicimus: Non quod PROPRIE corpus ejus sit panis, & poculum sanguis, sed quod in se MYSTERIUM corporis sanguinisque continent, secutus scil.
